title: A  dataset  recorded  during  development  of a  tempo-based  brain-computer  music  interface
description: EEG recordings from 19 healthy participants using a music-based brain-computer interface that lets users dynamically modulate music tempo through intentional control. Participants kinaesthetically imagined squeezing a ball with the right hand to increase tempo, or relaxed to decrease it. The paradigm comprised 9 runs, beginning with a calibration run of 30 trials in pairs of increase and decrease tempo trials.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 1 kHz from 19 participants. Each trial corresponded to a 20 s music clip generated by a synthetic affective music generator. The paradigm was split into 9 runs, the first being a calibration run of 30 trials alternating between increase and decrease tempo.
